source_text:
9.3 ολψμπιοδορι ιν
Εἰς τὸ κατ' ἐνέργειαν Ζωσίμου Τὸ δὲ ἅλας ἐπενοήθη ἐκ τῶν ἀρχαίων ἵνα μὴ κολληθῇ
ὁ ἀρσένικος εἰς τὸ ὑελοῦν κυθρίδιον, ὅπερ ὑελοῦν κυθρίδιον «ἀσύμποτον»
Ἀφρικανὸς ἐκάλεσεν.
pass_a_gloss: 9.3 Olympiodorus in Into the according-to-activity of-Zosimus. The but salt was-invented from the ancients so-that not should-stick the arsenic into the glass pot, which glass pot 'asympoton' Africanus called.
pass_b_english: Olympiodorus, in On Zosimus according to activity. Salt was invented by the ancients so that the arsenic should not stick to the glass pot, which glass pot Africanus called an asympoton.

lemmas.gloss: asympoton (Africanus's name for the glass pot)

choices.why: Keep the lock's vessel-name; do not paraphrase as 'undrinkable cup' without the term.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
